title: Read: tones and hanzi
description: Tones first, then about a hundred common hanzi with compound words.

units.title: The four tones
intro: Mandarin is written with characters called hanzi. Each character is one syllable and has a meaning.
Pinyin spells the sound of a character with Latin letters, like 'ma'. It is a helper, the same way romaji helps with Japanese.
The mark above the vowel is the tone: how your voice moves while you say the syllable. A different tone makes a different word.
1st tone (mā): high and flat, like holding one sung note. 2nd tone (má): rising, like asking 'what?'
3rd tone (mǎ): low and dipping, like a doubtful 'well...'. 4th tone (mà): a sharp fall, like a firm 'No!'
Neutral tone (ma): no mark. Short and light.
In this unit the same syllable, 'ma', is five different words. Listen to each one a few times before you move on.

items.hint: 1st tone: high and flat. The flat line over the a is the shape of your voice.
2nd tone: rising. The mark climbs upward, and so does your voice.

items.meaning: horse (3rd tone: dips low, then rises)
items.hint: 3rd tone: dips low. The mark is a small valley: go down, then a little up.
4th tone: sharp fall. The mark drops, like a scolding 'No!'
Neutral tone: light and short. Put 吗 at the end of a sentence to make it a yes/no question.

units.title: Numbers 1 to 5
intro: Numbers are a good first set of hanzi. The first three are just lines you can count.
Reading pinyin: 'yī' sounds like 'ee'. 'èr' sounds like 'are'. 'sān' sounds like 'sahn'.
'sì' is the tricky one: the i after s is not 'ee'. Say 's' and keep buzzing, like 'sz'. 'wǔ' sounds like 'woo'.
Watch the tone marks. They tell you how to move your voice, just like in the last unit.

items.hint: One line means one. 1st tone: high and flat, like the line itself.
Two lines mean two. 4th tone: falling.
Three lines mean three. 1st tone: high and flat.
A box with four sides, like a window with curtains. 4th tone: falling.
A shape standing between a top line and a bottom line. 3rd tone: dipping.

units.title: Numbers 6 to 10
intro: Five more and you can count to ten.
Reading pinyin: 'q' sounds like 'ch', so 'qī' is 'chee'. 'j' is a soft 'j', so 'jiǔ' is close to 'jyoh'.
'shí' is not 'she'. The i after sh sounds like 'r': say 'shr' with a rising voice. 'liù' is close to 'lyoh', 'bā' is 'bah'.
Then the fun part. Bigger numbers are built from pieces: 十一 is ten-one, which is 11. 二十 is two-ten, which is 20.

items.hint: A person with a hat, arms out and legs apart. 4th tone: falling.
Like an upside-down 7 with a line through it. 1st tone: high and flat.
Two strokes leaning apart. 1st tone: high and flat.
Close to a cross, but with a hooked tail: nine is almost ten. 3rd tone: dipping.
A cross, like a plus sign. 2nd tone: rising.

units.title: You and me
intro: Many hanzi are built from smaller parts, and the parts give clues. Watch the left side of the characters in this unit.
亻 on the left is a squeezed form of 人, person. 女 on the left means woman.
Reading pinyin: 'wǒ' is close to 'waw'. 'nǐ' is 'nee'. 'tā' is 'tah'. 'hǎo' is 'how'.
他 (he) and 她 (she) sound exactly the same. You can only tell them apart in writing.

items.hint: I, me. Many strokes, but you will see it so often it sticks. 3rd tone: dipping.
亻 (person) on the left: the person in front of me is you. 3rd tone: dipping.
亻 (person) on the left: he. 1st tone: high and flat.
女 (woman) on the left: she. Same sound as 他.
女 (woman) next to 子 (child): together they mean good. 3rd tone: dipping.

units.title: Small words
intro: Five characters that show up in almost every sentence.
Reading pinyin: 'rén' starts with a buzzing r, tongue curled back. 'dà' is 'dah'. 'xiǎo' is close to 'shyow': x is a soft sh.
是 is 'to be'. Mandarin uses the same word for am, is and are. No changes to memorize.
不 means 'not'. It is 'bù', but in front of another falling tone it flips to rising: 不是 is 'bú shì'.

items.hint: A person walking, seen from the side: two legs. 2nd tone: rising.
A person stretching both arms out wide: big. 4th tone: falling.
A center stroke with two small strokes falling away from it: small. 3rd tone: dipping.
To be. 日 (sun) sits on top. 'shr' with a sharp fall.
Not. A line on top, like a lid holding things down. 4th tone: falling.

units.title: Sun, moon, fire, water
intro: Some of the oldest hanzi started as drawings. These five still look a little like what they mean.
Reading pinyin: 'shuǐ' is close to 'shway'. 'huǒ' is 'hwaw'. 'shān' is 'shahn'. 'yuè' is 'yweh'.
'rì' is hard: curl your tongue back and buzz, like the r in 'run' held on its own, with a falling voice.
日 also means day, and 月 also means month. So 一月 is month one: January.

items.hint: A stream down the middle with splashes on both sides. 3rd tone: dipping.
A fire with a spark flying off each side. 3rd tone: dipping.
Three peaks: a mountain. 1st tone: high and flat.
It began as a circle with a dot: the sun. Also means day. 4th tone: falling.
A crescent moon standing upright. Also means month. 4th tone: falling.

units.title: Have, eat, drink
intro: Three everyday verbs and the name of the country.
口 is a mouth. Both 吃 (eat) and 喝 (drink) have it on the left.
Reading pinyin: 'yǒu' sounds like 'yo'. 'zhōng' is close to 'jong'. 'guó' is 'gwaw'. 'chī' is 'chr', high and flat. 'hē' is close to 'huh'.
中国 is 'middle country': China. Add 人 and you get 中国人, a Chinese person.

items.hint: To have. The bottom looks like 月. Picture a hand on top holding it. 3rd tone: dipping.
A line straight through the middle of a box: middle. 1st tone: high and flat.
A border around something precious: country. 2nd tone: rising.
口 (mouth) on the left: eat. 1st tone: high and flat.
口 (mouth) on the left again: drink. 1st tone: high and flat.

units.title: Family
intro: Family words are used every day, and most are doubled: 爸爸 (dad) and 妈妈 (mom). The second syllable is light.
Reading pinyin: 'bà' is 'bah'. 'gē' is close to 'guh'. 'jiě' is close to 'jyeh'. 'dì' is 'dee'. 'mèi' is 'may'.
姐 and 妹 both have 女 (woman) on the left, because they are sisters. 哥 and 弟 are brothers.

items.hint: 父 (father) on top gives the meaning. Say 'bah'. 4th tone: falling.
Two 可 stacked on top of each other: the big brother stands taller. 1st tone: high and flat.
女 (woman) on the left: a female relative. 3rd tone: dipping.
Picture a little brother with a topknot and a hook hanging down. 4th tone: falling.
女 (woman) on the left, like 姐: a female relative. 4th tone: falling.

units.title: School
intro: Five characters for school life. 学 is 'to study', and it also appears in 学生 (student) and 大学 (university).
Reading pinyin: 'xué' is close to 'shweh': x is a soft sh. 'shēng' is close to 'shung'. 'lǎo' is 'lao' as in 'now'. 'xiào' is close to 'shyow'.
老师 (lǎoshī) is 'old master': a teacher. Respect for age runs through many Chinese words.

items.hint: A child 子 sits under a roof of little marks: studying at home. 2nd tone: rising.
A sprout pushing up out of the ground: new life. 1st tone: high and flat.
A bent old person leaning on a stick. 3rd tone: dipping.
You will almost always see it in 老师, 'old master': a teacher. 1st tone: high and flat.
木 (wood) on the left. Together with 学 it makes 学校, school. 4th tone: falling.

units.title: Home and friends
intro: Two small grammar characters and three everyday words.
们 (men) makes a person word plural: 我 is I, 我们 is we. 的 (de) shows belonging: 我的家 is 'my home'. Both are light and short.
Reading pinyin: 'jiā' is 'jyah'. 'péng' is close to 'pung'. 'yǒu' is 'yo'.

items.hint: 亻 (person) on the left and 门 (door) on the right. Add it after 我, 你 or 他 to say we, you all, they. Neutral tone: light and short.
白 and a small 勺. Put it after a word: 我的 is mine, my. Neutral tone: light and short.
A roof over a pig: the pig was the family's wealth. Home. 1st tone: high and flat.
Two 月 side by side: two companions. 2nd tone: rising.
Two hands joined: friends. Said 'yo'. 3rd tone: dipping.

units.title: Food and drink
intro: Words for the table. 饭 can mean cooked rice, and also 'a meal' in general: 吃饭 is to eat.
Reading pinyin: 'fàn' is 'fahn'. 'chá' is 'chah'. 'mǐ' is 'mee'. 'ròu' starts with the buzzing r: close to 'roe'. 'cài' is 'tsai'.
好吃 (hǎochī) is 'good to eat': delicious. 好喝 (hǎohē) is 'good to drink'.

items.hint: 饣 (food) on the left. 吃饭 is to eat a meal. 4th tone: falling.
A plant 艹 on top, a person 人 in the middle, wood 木 below: someone picking tea leaves. 2nd tone: rising.
Grains of rice on a stalk, fanning out in all directions. 3rd tone: dipping.
A slab of meat with the marbling showing inside. 4th tone: falling.
艹 (grass) on top. Also means a dish on the table, as in 中国菜. 4th tone: falling.

units.title: Go, come, look, say, listen
intro: Five verbs you will use constantly. Mandarin verbs never change: 去 is go, whoever goes.
Reading pinyin: 'qù' is close to 'chyu': round your lips as for 'ü'. 'lái' is 'lie'. 'kàn' is 'kahn'. 'shuō' is 'shwaw'. 'tīng' is 'ting'.
说 and 听 both have a speech or mouth part on the left, because both belong to talking and hearing.

items.hint: The opposite of 来 (come). Say 'chyoo' with a sharp fall. 4th tone: falling.
A line down the middle with strokes on both sides, like someone with open arms coming toward you. 2nd tone: rising.
A hand 手 over an eye 目: a hand shading the eyes to look far. 4th tone: falling.
讠 (speech) on the left. 1st tone: high and flat.
口 (mouth) on the left and 斤 on the right. 说 is the speaking side, 听 is the listening side. 1st tone: high and flat.

units.title: Buy, do, want, write, read
intro: Five more verbs. 想 (xiǎng) is both 'to want' and 'to think': 想吃 is 'want to eat'.
Reading pinyin: 'mǎi' is 'my'. 'zuò' is close to 'dzwaw'. 'xiǎng' is close to 'shyahng'. 'xiě' is close to 'shyeh'. 'dú' is 'doo'.
买 (buy) and 卖 (sell, not taught yet) differ by one stroke on top. Keep them apart: the extra stroke is what you give away.

items.hint: Compare 卖 (mài, sell): the seller has one more stroke on top. 3rd tone: dipping.
亻 (person) on the left: a person doing something. 4th tone: falling.
心 (heart) at the bottom: what the heart wants and thinks. 3rd tone: dipping.
A cover on top of a base, like a brush resting over a page. 3rd tone: dipping.
讠 (speech) on the left: reading aloud. 2nd tone: rising.

units.title: Days and years
intro: Time words follow a pattern. 今 is this, 明 is next, 昨 is last: 今天 today, 明天 tomorrow, 昨天 yesterday.
Reading pinyin: 'nián' is close to 'nyen'. 'tiān' is close to 'tyen'. 'jīn' is 'jin'. 'míng' is 'ming'. 'zuó' is close to 'dzwaw'.
明 is a sun 日 and a moon 月 side by side: bright, then 'next', as in 明天.

items.hint: A long vertical stroke through the middle, like a stalk of grain: one harvest, one year. 2nd tone: rising.
大 (big) with a line over its head: the big sky above a person. 1st tone: high and flat.
A roof over a mark: this very moment. 1st tone: high and flat.
日 (sun) and 月 (moon) side by side: bright. Also 'next', as in 明天. 2nd tone: rising.
日 (sun, day) on the left: a day that has gone. 2nd tone: rising.

units.title: Parts of the day
intro: Words to say when. 上 is up and also 'before': 上午 is morning. 下 is down and also 'after': 下午 is afternoon.
To say the time, put the number before 点: 三点 is three o'clock. 分 is the minute: 五分 is five minutes.
Reading pinyin: 'shàng' is 'shahng'. 'xià' is close to 'shyah'. 'wǔ' is 'woo'. 'diǎn' is close to 'dyen'. 'fēn' is 'fun'.

items.hint: A short line above a long one: something on top. 4th tone: falling.
The reverse of 上: a short mark under a long line. 4th tone: falling.
The middle of the day. 中午 means 'the middle of the day': noon. 3rd tone: dipping.
Small dots underneath, like the dots on a clock face. 3rd tone: dipping.
八 (split) above 刀 (knife): to cut apart, a minute. 1st tone: high and flat.

units.title: Colours and amounts
intro: Two colours and two amounts, plus one more colour.
Reading pinyin: 'hóng' is close to 'hoong'. 'bái' is 'by'. 'hēi' is 'hay'. 'duō' is 'dwaw'. 'shǎo' is 'shao' as in 'now'.
多 is two 夕 (evening) stacked up, and it means many. 少 is 小 (small) with one more stroke, and it means few.

items.hint: 纟 (silk) on the left: red silk, a lucky colour. 2nd tone: rising.
A sun 日 with a small stroke on top, like the first white ray of dawn. 2nd tone: rising.
Four dots (fire) underneath: soot-black. 1st tone: high and flat.
Two 夕 stacked: evening after evening, many of them. 1st tone: high and flat.
小 (small) with one stroke through it: a small amount. 3rd tone: dipping.

units.title: Directions and cities
intro: The four compass points, and 京 (capital) to build city names with.
北京 (Běijīng) is 'northern capital', 南京 (Nánjīng) is 'southern capital', and 东京 (Dōngjīng) is Tokyo, 'eastern capital'.
Reading pinyin: 'dōng' is 'doong'. 'xī' is 'shee'. 'nán' is 'nahn'. 'běi' is 'bay'. 'jīng' is 'jing'.
东西 (dōngxi) means east and west, and also 'thing': you may be asked to buy 东西.

items.hint: Where the sun rises. 1st tone: high and flat.
Where the sun sets. 1st tone: high and flat.
A frame with a cross inside, like a house with a south-facing door. 2nd tone: rising.
Two people standing back to back: turning their backs to the south. 3rd tone: dipping.
A tall building with a roof: the great city, the capital. 1st tone: high and flat.

units.title: Tall, long, new, very
intro: Five words for describing things. 很 (hěn) is 'very' and you will use it all the time: 很好 is 'very good'.
In Mandarin, adjectives come right after 很, with no word for 'is': 我很好 is 'I am well'.
Reading pinyin: 'gāo' is 'gow' as in 'cow'. 'cháng' is 'chahng'. 'xīn' is 'sheen'. 'tài' is 'tie'. 'hěn' is close to 'hun'.

items.hint: A tall tower with a doorway below. 1st tone: high and flat.
A long, flowing line, like long hair. 2nd tone: rising.
斤 (axe) on the right: fresh wood just cut. 1st tone: high and flat.
大 (big) with an extra dot: too big. 4th tone: falling.
彳 (step) on the left. It shows up in almost every sentence with an adjective. 3rd tone: dipping.

units.title: This, that, a book
intro: 这 (this) and 那 (that) point at things. 个 (gè) and 本 (běn) are measure words: Mandarin counts things with a small word in between.
一个人 is 'one person'. 一本书 is 'one book'. 个 is the all-purpose measure word. 本 is for books.
Reading pinyin: 'zhè' is close to 'juh'. 'nà' is 'nah'. 'gè' is close to 'guh'. 'shū' is 'shoo'. 'běn' is close to 'bun'.
Careful with 一: before a falling tone it flips to rising (一个 is 'yí gè'), and before the other tones it falls (一本 is 'yì běn').

items.hint: 辶 (walk) at the bottom left: here, where you walk. Say 'juh' with a fall. 4th tone: falling.
The partner of 这: this is here, that is over there. Say 'nah' with a fall. 4th tone: falling.
A person 人 with a stroke: used to count people and many things. 4th tone: falling.
Simplified from 書, which has a brush in it: books are written with a brush. 1st tone: high and flat.
木 (tree) with a mark at the root: the root, and the word for counting books. 3rd tone: dipping.

units.title: Question words
intro: Question words take the place of the answer. 你是谁? 'Who are you?' is just 你是 with 谁 where the name goes. There is no need to rearrange the sentence.
What: 什么. Who: 谁. Which or where: 哪. Add 里 to 哪 for 'where': 哪里.
Reading pinyin: 'shén' is close to 'shun'. 'me' is light. 'shéi' is 'shay'. 'nǎ' is 'nah'. 'lǐ' is 'lee'.

items.hint: 亻 (person) on the left and 十 on the right. Used with 么 to ask 'what'. 2nd tone: rising.
A small hooked shape. It never stands alone, and is always light and short. Neutral tone: light and short.
讠 (speech) on the left: asking about a person. 2nd tone: rising.
口 (mouth) on the left: a mouth asking a question. 3rd tone: dipping.
田 (field) above 土 (earth): inside the land. In 哪里 it is light. 3rd tone: dipping.

where do you want to go
